## How to read it

The top of the table is the **NPC population**, not a random sample of the game's messages: `0x00F3`
and `0x00F6` (titles), `0x006D` (NPC weapons), `0x009B` (NPC name), `0x0056` and `0x0057`
(properties and model), `0x00A6` (profession). A live load spawns the map's agents and describes each
one; this server spawns the player and nobody else, so none of those messages exist to send. Building
them means giving the world an NPC population first - spawn points, models and names out of the
archive - which is the largest remaining piece of work here, and the one that changes most of what a
player sees.

Below that group are the one-off messages a load carries (`0x004C` quest description, `0x0121` and
`0x0127` guild info, `0x015E` an unnamed item form, `0x013A` a customized item name), then the
movement and property updates this server sends only some of (`0x002A` destination, `0x00A0` and
`0x00A3` targeted property updates, `0x002E` rotation).

```powershell
python tools/live-gaps.py            # rewrite this document
python tools/live-gaps.py --check    # fail when it is stale
```

69 message(s).
